systems.name: Oxygen Transport
systems.shortDescription: How blood carries oxygen to working tissues.
systems.overview: Oxygen transport links breathing, circulation, red blood cells, and energy use during activity.
systems.whyItMatters: Sustained exercise depends on coordinated lung, heart, blood, and muscle function.

systems.name: Muscle Contraction

systems.name: Sleep and Circadian Biology

systems.whyItMatters: Sleep records can make circadian regulation an interesting educational lens.

systems.name: Respiratory Biology

systems.whyItMatters: Breathing-related measurements can point toward educational modules about gas exchange.

systems.name: Cellular Energy

systems.overview: Metabolism includes glucose transport, ATP production, lactate handling, and hormone signaling.
systems.whyItMatters: Activity and energy expenditure are useful entry points for learning how cells manage fuel.

modules.title: How Hemoglobin Works
modules.summary: How hemoglobin binds oxygen, carries it through blood, and releases it in tissues.

steps.title: Oxygen binds to heme
steps.body: Oxygen can reversibly bind iron in heme groups within hemoglobin.

steps.title: Red blood cells carry it
steps.body: Red blood cells move hemoglobin through circulation so oxygen can reach distant tissues.

steps.title: Tissues favor release
steps.body: Local chemistry around active tissues can favor oxygen unloading from hemoglobin.

steps.title: Carbon dioxide shifts binding
steps.body: Carbon dioxide and pH influence oxygen release; the app does not measure hemoglobin activity.

modules.title: How Muscle Contraction Works
modules.summary: How ATP, calcium, actin, and myosin support movement.

steps.title: Calcium exposes binding sites
steps.body: Calcium signals shift regulatory proteins so myosin can interact with actin filaments.

steps.title: Myosin pulls actin
steps.body: Myosin heads bind actin and use ATP-linked shape changes to slide filaments past each other.

steps.title: ATP resets the motor
steps.body: ATP binding and hydrolysis detach and re-cock myosin so repeated cycles can generate force.

steps.title: Calcium returns to storage
steps.body: Calcium pumps help move calcium back into storage compartments so the fiber can relax.

modules.title: How Circadian Timing Works
modules.summary: How CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, and CRY proteins participate in daily timing.

steps.title: CLOCK and BMAL1 start transcription
steps.body: CLOCK and BMAL1 can partner to activate genes involved in the circadian cycle.

steps.title: PER and CRY accumulate
steps.body: PER and CRY proteins build up over time after their genes are expressed.

steps.title: Feedback slows the cycle
steps.body: Accumulated PER and CRY proteins help reduce CLOCK-BMAL1 activity, forming a feedback loop.

steps.title: Signals tune the rhythm
steps.body: Light exposure, sleep timing, and behavior can influence the timing signals that feed into this system.

modules.title: How Cellular Energy Works
modules.summary: How transporters, enzymes, and mitochondria turn fuel into ATP.

steps.title: Fuel enters the cell
steps.body: Transporters such as GLUT4 help move glucose into cells when the right signals are present.

steps.title: Glucose is processed in steps
steps.body: Enzymes convert glucose through intermediate molecules while capturing usable energy.

steps.title: Mitochondria make most ATP
steps.body: Mitochondrial enzyme complexes use fuel-derived electrons to support ATP production.

steps.title: Cells buffer quick demand
steps.body: Systems such as creatine kinase help smooth fast-changing energy demand in tissues like muscle.

modules.title: How Gas Exchange Works
modules.summary: How oxygen and carbon dioxide move between air, blood, and tissues.

steps.title: Air reaches exchange surfaces
steps.body: Breathing brings fresh air to thin exchange surfaces in the lungs.

steps.title: Oxygen moves into blood
steps.body: Oxygen moves from air spaces into nearby blood where it can bind transport proteins.

steps.title: Carbon dioxide moves out
steps.body: Carbon dioxide produced by tissues is carried back toward the lungs and released into exhaled air.

steps.title: Blood proteins support transport
steps.body: Hemoglobin and related proteins help coordinate oxygen delivery and carbon dioxide handling.
